triples.rationale: Israel is explicitly called to bless the Lord in the hymn; the psalm issues the same call to the house of Israel.
triples.source_text: Israel, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: House of Israel, bless the Lord; house of Aaron, bless the Lord.

triples.rationale: The hymn summons the Lord's priests to bless Him; the psalm calls the house of Aaron to bless Him. Exodus 28:1 explicitly appoints Aaron and his sons to priestly service, establishing the priestly household addressed by the psalm.
triples.source_text: Priests, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: House of Israel, bless the Lord; house of Aaron, bless the Lord.

triples.rationale: The hymn calls the Lord's servants to bless Him. The psalm likewise addresses all the Lord's slaves standing in His house and commands them to bless Him.
triples.source_text: Servants, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: A song of the ascents. Behold, bless the Lord, all slaves of the Lord, who stand in the Lord’s house, in the courts of the house of our God.

triples.relationship: shared description of the worshipping company
triples.rationale: The hymn includes the spirits and souls of righteous people among those blessing God. Hebrews describes the heavenly assembly as including the spirits of righteous ones made perfect, alongside angels and the assembly before God.
triples.source_text: Spirits and souls of the righteous, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: But you have approached Mount Zion and the city of the living God, heavenly Jerusalem, and myriads of angels in festive gathering,
and the assembly of firstborn ones enrolled in the heavens, and God the judge of all, and the spirits of righteous ones who have been perfected,

triples.rationale: The hymn summons holy people and the humble in heart to bless God. The psalm likewise calls the meek to hear and rejoice and invites them to magnify the Lord together.
triples.source_text: Holy ones and those humble in heart, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: My soul will be praised in the Lord; let the meek hear and rejoice.
Magnify the Lord with me; let us exalt His name together.

triples.rationale: The named companions thank God for rescue from death and the furnace. Their earlier answer had trusted His rescue and maintained their refusal to worship the king's idol.
triples.source_text: Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever. For He rescued us from Hades and saved us from the hand of death; He delivered us from the midst of the burning flame and redeemed us from the fire.

target_units.text: For there is a God in the heavens, our one Lord, whom we fear, who is able to rescue us from the furnace of fire; and from your hands, O king, He will rescue us.
Then it will be plain to you that we neither serve your idol nor bow to your golden image that you set up.”

triples.rationale: Both passages call for thanksgiving to the Lord because He is good or kind and His mercy is forever, joining the summons with the same enduring-mercy refrain.
triples.source_text: Give thanks to the Lord, for He is good, for His mercy endures for ever.

target_units.text: Hallelujah! Give thanks to the Lord, for He is kind; for His mercy is for ever.

triples.rationale: Both passages call for thanks to the God of gods and give His everlasting mercy as the refrain. The divine title and the reason for thanksgiving correspond.
triples.source_text: Bless, all who revere the God of gods; sing praise and give thanks, for His mercy endures for ever and for the age of ages.”

target_units.text: Give thanks to the God of gods; for His mercy is for ever.

triples.relationship: same-chapter audible hymn and royal response
triples.rationale: The king hears the men singing and sees them alive. The earlier account identified the three men beginning their hymn in one voice, supplying the singing to which he reacts.
triples.source_text: When the king heard them singing and, standing, observed them alive, King Nebuchadnezzar was astonished, rose in haste, and said to his friends:

target_units.text: Then the three took up the song as with one mouth, singing hymns, glorifying, blessing, and exalting God in the furnace, saying:

triples.rationale: The king sees four unharmed, unbound figures and describes the fourth as angelic. The narrator has already described the Lord's angel joining the three and the furnace becoming harmless to them.
triples.source_text: “Behold! I see four men unbound, walking in the fire, and no harm has come upon them. The fourth has the likeness of an angel of God.”

target_units.text: An angel of the Lord descended into the furnace together with Azariah and his companions and shook the flame of fire out of the furnace.
He made the middle of the furnace like a dew-laden breeze whistling through. The fire did not touch them at all; it neither distressed nor troubled them.

triples.rationale: The king now calls the three men out of the fire as servants of the Most High. Earlier he had ordered those same men bound and thrown into it; his new command reverses their confinement.
triples.source_text: The king approached the door of the furnace blazing with fire and called them by name: “Sedrach, Misach, and Abdenago, servants of the Most High God of gods, come out of the fire!” Thus the men came out from the midst of the fire.

target_units.text: He ordered the strongest men in his force to bind Sedrach, Misach, and Abdenago hand and foot and throw them into the blazing furnace.
Then those men were bound hand and foot, wearing their footwear and the tiaras on their heads, together with their clothing, and were thrown into the furnace.

triples.relationship: shared promise and narrative of preservation in fire
triples.rationale: The inspection finds no burning of the men's bodies or hair and no fire damage to their clothing. Isaiah's assurance to Israel describes passing through fire without being burned up, sharing the particular motif of preservation in fire narrated here.
triples.source_text: The consuls, district governors, ancestral chiefs, and the king’s friends gathered. They observed those men: the fire had not touched their bodies, their hair had not burned, their trousers were unchanged, and there was no smell of fire on them.

target_units.text: Even if you cross through water, I am with you, and rivers will not flood over you. Even if you pass through fire, you will certainly not be burned up; flame will not burn you up.

triples.relationship: same-chapter confession confirming the companions' answer
triples.rationale: The king credits their God and His angel with rescue and recalls their refusal to worship another god. Both rescue and exclusive allegiance were expressed in the companions' earlier answer to him.
triples.source_text: King Nebuchadnezzar spoke and said, “Blessed be the Lord, the God of Sedrach, Misach, and Abdenago, who sent His angel and saved His servants who hoped in Him. They rejected the king’s command and surrendered their bodies to burning so that they would neither serve nor bow to another god except their own God.

target_units.text: For there is a God in the heavens, our one Lord, whom we fear, who is able to rescue us from the furnace of fire; and from your hands, O king, He will rescue us.
Then it will be plain to you that we neither serve your idol nor bow to your golden image that you set up.”

triples.rationale: The king now declares that no other god can rescue in this way. This answers his earlier challenge asking what god could rescue the companions from his hands.
triples.source_text: Now I decree: from every nation, every tribe, and every language, whoever blasphemes the Lord, the God of Sedrach, Misach, and Abdenago, will be dismembered and his house confiscated, because there is no other god who can rescue like this.”

target_units.text: Now, if you are ready, as soon as you hear the trumpet and every musical sound, to fall down and bow to the golden image I set up—but if not, know that unless you bow, you will immediately be thrown into the blazing furnace. What god will rescue you from my hands?”

triples.rationale: The king grants the three companions authority over the country after their rescue. Earlier Daniel had petitioned for them to be appointed over Babylonia's affairs; the passages trace his request and their subsequent royal service without equating the precise rank of each notice.
triples.source_text: Thus the king gave Sedrach, Misach, and Abdenago authority over the whole country and appointed them rulers.

target_units.text: Daniel petitioned the king that Sedrach, Misach, and Abdenago be appointed over Babylonia’s affairs. Daniel remained in the royal court.
